title: mRNA Extraction from Gill Tissue for RNA-sequencing
author: Jukka-Pekka Verta
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML

steps.title: Euthanize fish and dissect gills
steps.instruction: Prepare a 10× MS‑222 solution (1.5 g L⁻¹ MS‑222 and 3.0 g L⁻¹ NaHCO₃ in aquarium water, pH 7.5). Anesthetize the stickleback by overdose, remove the head with scalpel and forceps, open the operculum ventrally, excise the gill arches from ventral and dorsal attachments, trim away non‑gill connective tissue, collect ~50 mg of gill tissue into a 1.5 ml RNase‑free Safe‑Lock tube, snap‑freeze immediately in liquid nitrogen and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare Dynabeads and solutions
steps.instruction: Allow Dynabeads and all buffers (lysis, Wash‑A, Wash‑B) to reach room temperature. Aliquot 100 µl Dynabeads into each 1.5 ml tube, place on a DynaMag‑2 magnet for ~30 s, discard the supernatant, then resuspend the beads in 100 µl of lysis buffer (the original volume of the beads).

steps.title: Modify and chill pestles
steps.instruction: Cut the round conical surface of each Micro‑Tube homogenizing pestle into an angular shape with sterile scissors or a scalpel, then dip the pestle in liquid nitrogen to cool before use.

steps.title: Homogenize frozen tissue to powder
steps.instruction: Keep frozen gill samples on liquid nitrogen, insert the cooled pestle into each tube and grind the tissue to a fine powder while maintaining the sample frozen; avoid any melting before the lysis step.

steps.title: Lyse cells and shear DNA
steps.instruction: While the tube is still frozen, add 250 µl lysis buffer, immediately drop the pestle back in and grind until the frozen buffer melts, ensuring the tissue is fully suspended. Discard the pestle and pass the lysate five times through a 21 G needle to shear genomic DNA.

steps.title: Bind mRNA to Dynabeads
steps.instruction: Add 100 µl of the washed and resuspended Dynabeads to each lysate, incubate for 5 min at room temperature with continuous rotation (~500 rpm) to promote mRNA binding while minimizing genomic DNA attachment.

steps.title: Wash bead‑mRNA complex (Wash‑A)
steps.instruction: Place tubes on the magnet for ~30 s, remove all supernatant, resuspend beads in 600 µl room‑temperature Wash‑A buffer, and repeat the magnet‑wash cycle for a second Wash‑A (a third Wash‑A may be performed for higher purity). Fully resuspend beads by slow pipetting; avoid clumps and excessive shearing.

substeps.instruction: First Wash‑A: 600 µl Wash‑A, magnet 30 s, discard supernatant.
Optional third Wash‑A: repeat as above.

steps.title: Wash bead‑mRNA complex (Wash‑B)
steps.instruction: After the final Wash‑A, resuspend beads in 300 µl room‑temperature Wash‑B buffer, place on magnet for ~30 s, and remove all supernatant without disturbing the bead pellet.

steps.title: Elute mRNA from beads
steps.instruction: Place tubes on the magnet for ~30 s, discard residual buffer, resuspend beads in 20 µl RNase‑free water, incubate 2 min at 65 °C (thermocycler or thermomixer), immediately re‑magnetize and transfer the supernatant containing eluted mRNA to a fresh RNase‑free 1.5 ml tube.

steps.title: Treat eluted mRNA with DNase
steps.instruction: To the 20 µl eluted mRNA add 2 µl Turbo DNase buffer and 1 µl Turbo DNase, incubate 20 min at 37 °C. Then add 5 µl DNase inactivation solution, flick gently, incubate 5 min at room temperature, spin 1 min 30 s at 10 000 × g, and transfer the cleared supernatant to a new RNase‑free tube. Snap‑freeze aliquots (e.g., 10 µl) in liquid nitrogen and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Optional qPCR check for DNA contamination
steps.instruction: Design primers for a single‑exon housekeeping gene (e.g., claudin: Fwd 5'‑ACTTGGTGCCCTATCAAATGAGGTA‑3', Rev 5'‑AGTTATACACGACGGGAGGATTGAG‑3'). Reverse‑transcribe 5 µl mRNA with 3 µl water and 2 µl PrimeScript RT Master Mix, incubate 15 min at 37 °C, store at –20 °C. Prepare qPCR mix per reaction: 10 µl 2× SYBR Select Master Mix, 1 µl 10 mM forward primer, 1 µl 10 mM reverse primer, 2 µl water, 1 µl cDNA. Run program: 50 °C 2 min, 95 °C 2 min, then 30 s at 95 °C, 30 s at 55‑65 °C (primer‑specific), 30 s at 72 °C, repeat for 39 cycles, hold 4 °C. Absence of amplification indicates successful DNase treatment.

steps.title: Assess mRNA quality with Bioanalyzer
steps.instruction: Quantify mRNA (Qubit RNA BR or Bioanalyzer RNA 6000 Nano; use RNA 6000 Pico if concentration < ~5 ng µl⁻¹). Load the sample on an Agilent Bioanalyzer using the RNA 6000 Nano kit, evaluate the fragment‑size distribution (high‑molecular‑weight mRNA peaks indicate good quality; a left‑shifted distribution indicates degradation). Note that RIN is not applicable for mRNA‑only samples.

steps.title: Construct Illumina TruSeq RNA‑seq library
steps.instruction: Using the Illumina TruSeq Stranded mRNA kit, input 150 ng of the DNase‑treated mRNA (adjust volume to 50 µl with RNase‑free water). Follow the kit’s instructions, except fragment the RNA for 2 min (optimised for 150 bp paired‑end HiSeq 3000 reads to obtain ~290 bp inserts). Use the supplied indexes for each sample, pool libraries in equimolar amounts, and sequence. If possible, use a unique index per sample and sequence all libraries in the same lane to avoid batch effects; replicate lanes may be combined for deeper coverage.
